title: Effects of annealing and pulsed current treatment on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Cu/Al2O3 deposits prepared by cold spray

preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Material_Composition: 0.03 wt% Cu, 0.12 wt% Si, 0.01 wt% Mn, 0.02 wt% Mg, 0.03 wt% Zn, 0.02 wt% Ti, 0.14 wt% Fe, Bal. Al

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: samples were separated from the deposits along the scanning direction by electric discharge wire cutting for subsequent treatments. samples were observed after 8–10 s of erosion using an etchant (96 ml anhydrous ethanol + 3 g FeCl3 + 2 ml HCl)

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: microstructure of the as sprayed materials was quite compact and no obvious defects were found. relatively uniform Al2O3 distribution, at 6.81 vol% Al2O3. bonding between the Cu particles, Cu and Al2O3 particles, was mainly simple mechanical interlocking

preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Material_Composition: 0.03 wt% Cu, 0.12 wt% Si, 0.01 wt% Mn, 0.02 wt% Mg, 0.03 wt% Zn, 0.02 wt% Ti, 0.14 wt% Fe, Bal. Al

experimentalProperties.Deposit_Post_Treatment_Description: Annealed in a muffle furnace with argon gas, heated to 300°C with a heating rate of 10°C/min for 2h once the target temperature was reached. Cooled to room temperature in the furnace.
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: samples were separated from the deposits along the scanning direction by electric discharge wire cutting for subsequent treatments. samples were observed after 8–10 s of erosion using an etchant (96 ml anhydrous ethanol + 3 g FeCl3 + 2 ml HCl)

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: remained dense and did not change significantly compared to the as sprayed samples. weak particle boundaries

preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Material_Composition: 0.03 wt% Cu, 0.12 wt% Si, 0.01 wt% Mn, 0.02 wt% Mg, 0.03 wt% Zn, 0.02 wt% Ti, 0.14 wt% Fe, Bal. Al

experimentalProperties.Deposit_Post_Treatment_Description: Annealed in a muffle furnace with argon gas, heated to 500°C with a heating rate of 10°C/min for 2h once the target temperature was reached. Cooled to room temperature in the furnace.
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: samples were separated from the deposits along the scanning direction by electric discharge wire cutting for subsequent treatments. samples were observed after 8–10 s of erosion using an etchant (96 ml anhydrous ethanol + 3 g FeCl3 + 2 ml HCl)

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: remained dense and did not change significantly compared to the as sprayed samples. bonding interfaces between most of the Cu particles had been healed effectively, but bonding between Cu and Al2O3 particles did not undergo significant changes.

preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Material_Composition: 0.03 wt% Cu, 0.12 wt% Si, 0.01 wt% Mn, 0.02 wt% Mg, 0.03 wt% Zn, 0.02 wt% Ti, 0.14 wt% Fe, Bal. Al

experimentalProperties.Deposit_Post_Treatment_Description: Annealed in a muffle furnace with argon gas, heated to 700°C with a heating rate of 10°C/min for 2h once the target temperature was reached. Cooled to room temperature in the furnace.
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: samples were separated from the deposits along the scanning direction by electric discharge wire cutting for subsequent treatments. samples were observed after 8–10 s of erosion using an etchant (96 ml anhydrous ethanol + 3 g FeCl3 + 2 ml HCl)

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: micro-cracks appeared inside. the Cu/Al2O3 interface also did not develop metallurgical bonding, and had the presence of pores, cracks, and a weak Cu/Al2O3 interface.
